references.text: The burnt offering was to be a bull from the cattle, a male without defect, as described here with 'par echad ben-bakar' (one bull, a young one from the cattle).
A burnt offering of small livestock, either from the sheep or the goats, was to be a male without defect, corresponding to the rams and lambs mentioned in this verse.
At the dedication of the tabernacle, a calf and a ram were also offered as a burnt offering, the same types of animals mentioned here.
A one-year-old lamb for a burnt offering is also mentioned in connection with the sin offering, corresponding to 'kevesh echad ben-shenato' (one lamb, one year old).
On the day of the new moon, two young bulls, one ram, and seven one-year-old lambs were to be offered as a burnt offering, similar to the animals described here.
The Passover sacrifice also included young bulls, rams, and one-year-old lambs for a burnt offering, corresponding to this verse.
On the day of trumpet blowing, one young bull, one ram, and seven one-year-old lambs were to be offered as a burnt offering, the same types of animals as in Numbers 7:15.
The daily burnt offering consisted of one-year-old lambs, corresponding to 'kevesh echad ben-shenato' mentioned here.
